result.rationale: The diff shows `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` in embed.js, which validates the message sender by substring containment rather than strict origin equality. An origin that is a substring of discourseUrl (e.g., a distinct host whose origin string happens to prefix-match) would pass the check, letting a malicious page manipulate the iframe's height. The mechanism is verifiable in the diff; impact is limited (only iframe height control), so confidence is moderate.

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, postMessageReceived filters messages with `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`, which is a substring containment check rather than an origin equality check. This means any `e.origin` that is contained within the configured `discourseUrl` string will be accepted, which is weaker than intended origin validation for postMessage and can allow unintended origins to control the iframe height (`iframe.height = ...`).
